a.clause: §2(a) licence + §2(b) ("create, test, manage and optimize voice agents"); no competitive-use or benchmarking clause
a.note: The licence is "solely for the purpose of deploying AI voice agents". Building and test-calling an agent fits that, but an evaluation that never intends to deploy sits at its edge.

b.clause: §2(d) item 8: "use any robot, spider, crawler, scraper, avatar, miner or other manual or automated means to access the Services"
b.note: The API is the sanctioned automated channel (§2(a) Documentation). Driving the dashboard with Playwright is an "automated means to access the Services". The trailing "doesn't relate to Your Content" qualifier could be read as narrowing the list, but the first limb stands on its own.

c.clause: §2(d) item 7: "reverse engineer, duplicate, decompile, disassemble, or decode any part of the Vapi Software ... or otherwise extract the source code"
c.note: The JS bundle is "client-side software ... for you to ... execute as part of the Services". Source maps are literally extracted source. Passive network-tab viewing is less clear ("decode any part of ... the Services").

d.clause: Not addressed; nearest is §2(d) item 14: "leverage the Service to produce datasets for ... developing templates or products for third-party"
d.note: No clause bars learning from the product or building a competitor. The risk is item 14. Teardown artefacts such as timing tables, transcript corpora and claims files are datasets produced with the Service, and VP's product is for third parties. Taking away patterns only, with no dataset, is the lowest-risk reading.

notes: §6.2 is a standalone promise, not a restriction on how the Product is used: "will not ... build a product or service which competes with the Product". On its words it binds VP for as long as VP is an Exotel customer under these terms, including if VP only buys Exotel telephony for its own platform.

Whether VP "competes with the Product" is a fact question. Clause 1 defines the Product as Exophone numbers, the platform/UI/APIs, the browser extension/SDK, the mobile app and documentation, and describes calls, IVR and SMS. Exotel's site also sells AI Voice Agents, but this agreement does not name them.

Cross-references inside the agreement are off by one in places (e.g. it cites 'clause 21.2 (Termination)' and 'clause 17 (Confidentiality Obligations)', but the headings are 20.2 and 16). That makes it harder to interpret.
No reverse-engineering, scraping, automation or benchmarking clause exists in this agreement.

a.clause: §6.2: "or build a product or service which competes with the Product" (standalone covenant); §3(a): "for business communication purposes"
a.note: Test calls are ordinary use. But §6.2 is breached by building a competitor at all, not by any particular use of the trial. So the answer turns on whether VP "competes with the Product" as clause 1 defines it. If it does, VP cannot be an Exotel customer under these terms in good standing, and §20.2(b)(ii) allows immediate termination on an alleged breach.
